topicName: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Matrix Authorization
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Matrix Authorization in Jenkins"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Securing your Jenkins server is crucial for maintaining a reliable CI/CD pipeline. By default, Jenkins allows new installations to secure nothing or use basic user database authentication. To implement enterprise-grade security, you must configure authorization strategies. This tutorial covers Matrix-based authorization and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) using the popular Role-based Authorization Strategy plugin."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A running Jenkins instance with administrative access."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The Role-based Authorization Strategy plugin installed via Manage Jenkins -> Plugins."},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Enabling Matrix-based Security"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Matrix-based security allows you to grant specific global permissions to users and groups using a grid interface. To enable it, navigate to Manage Jenkins -> Security, and select 'Matrix-based security' under the Authorization section."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"User/Group | Overall:Admin | Job:Read | Job:Create | SCM:Checkout
-------------------------------------------------------------
anonymous  | [ ]         | [ ]      | [ ]        | [ ]        
authenticated | [ ]      | [x]      | [ ]        | [x]        
developers | [ ]         | [x]      | [x]        | [x]        "},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the matrix above, 'authenticated' users can read jobs and checkout code, while 'developers' have additional permissions to create jobs. Always ensure your admin user has full permissions before saving."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Transitioning to Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"While Matrix authorization is powerful, it becomes difficult to manage as your organization scales. RBAC solves this by grouping permissions into roles and assigning users to those roles. Go back to Manage Jenkins -> Security and select 'Role-Based Strategy'."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Configuring Global and Project Roles"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the Role-Based Strategy is active, a new option named 'Manage and Assign Roles' appears under Manage Jenkins. Click it to define your permission sets."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Global roles apply across the entire Jenkins instance (e.g., Admin, Read-Only, Build Agent Manager)."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Project roles restrict access to specific jobs using regular expression patterns (e.g., 'qa-.*' for jobs starting with qa-)."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"Role Name  | Pattern | Overall:Read | Job:Read | Job:Build | Job:Workspace
--------------------------------------------------------------------
QA-Team    | qa-.*   | [x]          | [x]      | [x]       | [x]          
Dev-Team   | dev-.*  | [x]          | [x]      | [x]       | [x]          "},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Assigning Users to Roles"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"After creating roles, navigate to the 'Assign Roles' section in the same menu. Add your users or external identity provider (LDAP/Active Directory) groups, and check the boxes corresponding to the roles they should inherit."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"User/Group | admin | QA-Team | Dev-Team
--------------------------------------
john_doe   | [x]   | [ ]     | [ ]     
sarah_qa   | [ ]   | [x]     | [ ]     
bob_dev    | [ ]   | [ ]     | [x]     "},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"You have successfully implemented granular security in Jenkins using Matrix Authorization and Role-Based Access Control. This ensures that users only have access to the specific tools, views, and jobs necessary to perform their roles, greatly reducing the risk of accidental or malicious alterations to your CI/CD pipelines."}]
